gloss: The artifacts selected to travel, grouped by delivery route and linked back to the inventory that owns each one.
narrative: Reads docs/portable.csv. Each row names its kind (skill, document, directory, or standalone tool) and links to the Skills, Docs, or Automation inventory that owns it. A row's title opens the file in the swipe deck the Docs tab uses; a directory row opens its folder, and every row's GitHub icon opens the source peek. The tab carries its own search box.

gloss: The primitives that make a session's work visible in chat, which is the only channel out of a sandbox.
narrative: Reads docs/surfacing.csv, which indexes the primitives of docs/SURFACING.md. A door under the header leads to each of that document's other regions and says when each one reaches a session. The header's Read control opens the document in the Docs tab's swipe deck, so a docked reader sees the prose beside the cards rather than in place of them.

gloss: Which link reaches which kind of change, what each one cannot show, and the address grammar behind all of them.
narrative: Reads docs/showing-mechanisms.csv for the mechanisms and what each misses, then docs/routes.json for the address grammar, docs/routes-modes.csv for toss-render's delivery modes and their trust postures, and docs/routes-routes.csv for the toss routes. The rule for picking a mechanism is executable rather than written here: npm run showing reads a branch's changed files and prints the link that reaches them.

gloss: Every document in the folder: what it is about, whether it still claims to be true, and who can reach it.
narrative: Reads docs/docs.csv. Each row gives a document's subject, status (living, record, or measured), reach (injected, in context, by a skill, by the app, or orphan), size in words with its share of the folder, and readership: the distinct sessions that opened the file, read from the private registry's sessions cache and shown only with a token. Maintenance fields sit behind one details toggle. A folder rail rolls up counts and words. A row's title opens the document in a fullscreen swipe deck over its folder; the GitHub icon opens the source peek.

gloss: The mission this estate's material serves, the five goals it is held to, and the paths into its documentation.
narrative: Renders docs/aims.json, which holds the mission sentence, with docs/aims-goals.csv for the goals and docs/aims-reading.csv for the ordered reading paths. The paths begin with the repository README, the agent contract, and the docs index. Addressed as ?tab=aims, its key from when it was a top-level tab.

gloss: Every document's length across the repository's history, drawn as motion rather than left as a number.
narrative: Charts the doc-growth payload (data/doc-growth/*.json) of every repository that declares a growth path in its .web-tools.json, the hub included. The hub's payload is a public fetch, so the chart renders without a token; the selector between repositories needs one.

gloss: What this estate says more than once: every repetition its prose actually contains, and the few anyone has accounted for.
refs: every repetition its prose actually contains=docs/themes.csv;the few anyone has accounted for=docs/owners.csv
narrative: Reads docs/themes.csv, the measured pairs of files sharing repeated prose, and docs/owners.csv, the curated statements. Four lenses over the duplication graph (clusters, an arc diagram, the repeated passages, and a matrix) share one threshold on shared 10-word shingles. Owners shows each repeated statement's authoritative file and its repetitions. Related reads data/doc-overlap/, passage embeddings kept apart from the shingles: each pair's share of matched passage words in both directions, with the passages side by side. Pairs with a passage under 20 words are hidden until asked for, and matches from cosine 0.85 are marked likely restating. Named Claims until 2026-08-09 and Owners until 2026-08-31.

gloss: Every executable the repository runs on itself, by the route execution arrives on: asked for, or fired by an environment build or a git, session, hook, or CI event.
narrative: The Automation subview. Reads docs/harness.csv: an authored role per file, plus derived layer, line count, invocation route, whether the file writes files, whether prose names it, and whether a test exercises it. A route is pulled (npm script, scenario driver, imported helper, argv), event-fired (env:build, git:<name>, session:SessionStart, hook:<event>, ci:<events>), or none found, which renders as a warning. A folder rail mirrors the tree on disk with counts and blank roles rolled up; the invocation pills filter on top of it.

gloss: Every check in the suite, what it holds to what, and what would go unnoticed if it were deleted.
narrative: Reads docs/tests.csv. Each check has an authored kind (gate or behavior) and a statement of what breaks without it; assertion count, method, runner, and boot-smoke count are derived from the files and gated against the registry. The strip splits the total by kind. A browser-driven check shows no assertion count rather than zero, since it asserts in its own harness.

gloss: Everything that enters a session, grouped by where it is defined, with who can change it and where two sources overlap.
refs: Everything that enters a session=docs/context-sources.csv;where it is defined=docs/context.md
narrative: Reads docs/context-sources.csv, the public half, and with a token the private half, web-tools-private's environment/context-sources.csv, which shares its columns; docs/context-topics.csv supplies the topics sources are compared on. Sources sit in circles by where they are defined, outermost first: the claude.ai account, the cloud environment, user scope, the plugin, the repo, the session. Four lenses read them: Circles; When, which places each source by the moment it arrives and lights the sources of a picked topic; Overlaps; and Measured, which reads the session store's tally. A private circle without a token says so rather than rendering empty.

gloss: Every browser JavaScript module under lib/kits/*.js: what its own header says it is, what loads it, and whether a demo shows it running.
narrative: Reads docs/kits.csv, which is wholly derived. The namespace and gloss come from each file's header comment; then whether every chain-boot page pays for the kit, whether a demo page exists (opened in-app as an app view), how many files load it, and whether a test names it. The strip filters on those. Three warning states render in the warning tone rather than being hidden: a blank gloss, a blank namespace, and a kit nothing loads.

gloss: The dimensions the UI units are coded on, the codes each one sorts them into, and where every unit falls on each.
narrative: The landing of UI. Reads data/ui-units/: dimensions.csv for the six dimensions (body, frame, reach, binding and phone, which readers code against codebook.md, and ring, which tools/ui-units.mjs computes), codes.csv for the codes of each, and coded.csv and units.csv for every unit's values. budget-drs units come from home's data/ui-units/ under a token. By dimension, each dimension states what it holds, whether a unit takes one code or any number, and each code's share of the units, opening to its gloss and its units. As a table, one row per unit and one column per dimension, sorted by any column.

gloss: A screenshot of every coded UI unit with its slots outlined and named, grouped by one dimension at a time.
narrative: The Gallery subview of UI. Reads the same tables as Dimensions, plus thumbs/thumbs.csv for each unit's desktop and phone shot and instances.csv for the pattern a unit's markup declares and whether it held when checked; budget-drs shots come from web-tools-private's thumbs/ under a token, and a link's refs= selection reaches their branches. One section per code of the chosen dimension, each unit a card that opens its section as a deck. Under a body code, the section says which kit draws it and how many units declare it. A warning edge marks a unit whose own code does a job a shared kit already does.

gloss: Every skill a session can reach, across the three sets they arrive from, what carrying each set costs, and the outside skills followed or copied.
narrative: The sets are Plugin, read from docs/portable.csv; Library, the on-demand skills in skills/manifest.csv; Estate, the skills other repositories declare, read from the crawled config cache and shown only with a token; and Outside, docs/upstream-skills.csv, the skills written elsewhere that the estate watches, studies, holds under outside/ or copies into skills/, each with the version pinned. A copied skill's Plugin or Library row names where it came from. A segmented control picks the set, and the line under it states what carrying that set costs a session. The Library's subject groups filter it, with counts that re-weight under the search box.

gloss: The tracked CSV files each repository declares, with their paths, physical dimensions, and column headers.
narrative: Reads the census file each repository names in its .web-tools.json data.census key: the hub's own data/csv-census.csv, and, with a token, those of estate repositories found in the crawled config cache. Each census lists tracked CSV paths, headers, and physical measurements. A file opens in the Files view, where a CSV renders as a filterable table.

gloss: Every address the app can be sent to, ranked by when the code behind it last moved, and what is open against it now.
refs: Every address the app can be sent to=docs/app-routes.csv
narrative: Joins docs/app-routes.csv to the hub's own history: each route's files are dated by their last commit, and open pull requests touching those files are listed against it. It needs a token, and says so without one. The census line counts routes, routes with no file of their own, and routes with work open. The former address ?view=routes forwards here.

gloss: The declaration table the other tabs hang off: for each committed inventory, what it covers and what holds it to its subject.
narrative: Reads docs/registries.csv with docs/properties.csv and docs/vocabularies.csv. One card per registry, grouped by area (files or names), shows its title, gloss, path, gate, target, scope, and a chip per declared property, with totals derived rather than written. Each card lists its renders_in files, the app files that name the registry in code, as peekable links; a registry no app surface reads gets a warning badge and a figure in the strip.

gloss: The rules the documentation settles, grouped into topics, each with the passage that states it and, where known, who set it.
narrative: Reads docs/policies.csv and docs/policy-topics.csv. A first pass, built 2026-10-01 from a Gemini prototype (web-tools #850) and filled by Haiku readers over the living docs and the governance skills; the suite holds every quoted passage to its document. The rail groups topics under six areas, and the filters split rules by level (principle, policy, standard) and by origin, which is unknown for most rows. The 15 rows carried from the prototype quote session prompts that remain unverified.

gloss: The places outside git that hold estate material: what declares each one's contents, how its state is observed and by whom, the check, and the upkeep.
narrative: Reads docs/outposts.csv, one card per outpost: its declaration, where its observation comes from and who supplies it, the check that compares them, the upkeep that restores it, and where dated observations are committed. The account card also reads docs/account-skills.csv and, with a token, web-tools-private environment/account-skills.csv, the observation a session last wrote with skills/hooks/account-skills.py --write, listing each skill's state with the ones needing attention first. The live check is that script's session-start hook; the list is only as current as the date it shows.
